video.title: You Can Feel This - Here's How

classification.reason: The coach gives explicit mental cues and internal checks, instructing the player to intend to pull the hip backwards while driving the shoulders forward to load the fascial chain.

problem.title_as_question: Why should you intend to pull your pelvis backwards during the forehand when it physically rotates forward?
problem.definition: Players often attempt to actively drive their hitting hip forward through the forehand, which paradoxically destroys elastic stretch tension across the torso and prevents an effective kinetic energy handoff into the shoulders.
prerequisites: Unit turn coiling prior to forward swing
problem.target_player: Players struggling with rotational power transfer or over-rotating their hips and shoulders together

symptoms.description: The hips and shoulders rotate forward together in-phase without creating torso separation or elastic stretch.
Lack of an elastic loading feel where the pelvis is yanked backwards while the shoulder is pulled forward.
Reduced forehand pace and lack of effortless rotational whip during the energy handoff.

causes.statement: Consciously trying to drive the hip forward through the shot makes the brain avoid stretching the connective tissue that would brake the pelvis, causing the hips and shoulders to turn together without stretch.
The oblique and fascial chain connecting the hip and shoulder generates equal and opposite tension, meaning any elastic force pulling the shoulder forward inherently pulls the hip backward.
The physical forward firing of the pelvis exists biomechanically to pre-stretch the fascial tissue to generate maximum backward-pulling force before the shoulders overtake it.
The backward acceleration applied to the pelvis decelerates its forward velocity rather than visibly reversing its direction, making the backward pulling force difficult to see on video.

angles.summary: The external oblique and fascial line connecting hip and shoulder stretch when hips and shoulders twist opposite, storing elastic energy that unstretches reciprocally.
Humans do not directly perceive spatial motion but rather perceive tension and acceleration, which feels like the hip being yanked backward as the shoulders fling forward.
The coach uses a twisting corkscrew model with two anchors to illustrate how pulling shoulders forward physically pulls the hip anchor backward.
Coaches often tell players to send the hip forward through the shot, but following this advice causes the body to deliberately avoid creating elastic torso stretch.

solutions.summary: Intend to take the hitting hip side and fire it backwards as you begin to initiate rotation into the forehand.
Use the internal cue 'drive shoulders forward, hips back' from your coiled state to create full torso stretch tension.
Practice shifting the pelvis forward initially solely to prime and maximize the backward-pulling elastic force that fires through the hip.
Check that you distinctly feel your pelvis under elastic tension being yanked backwards as the shoulder accelerates forward, even if the hip still moves forward.
